# Does an AI handoff mean a software purchase was completed?

A handoff marks the task's endpoint, not a completed software purchase. Agent Gap recorded 163 reached outcomes across 210 initial website tasks on 6 October 2026. That result does not supply a count of submitted forms, booked meetings, paid orders or deployed products.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Agent Gap endpoint method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) recorded three public website tasks across 70 selected vendors. The reached counts were 67 of 70 for Describe, 52 of 70 for Pricing page and 44 of 70 for Demo path, adding to 163 of 210 initial sessions. Thirty preselected repeats were reported separately.

The task labels matter. The combined 163 includes description and pricing work as well as demo paths; it must not be presented as 163 purchases or even 163 demo requests. The study recorded distinct discovery, correctness and endpoint fields.

Its 6 October 2026 observations do not establish a transaction-completion rate or later buyer behavior.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read the stopping condition before quoting the success count. If the task stops at a page, call it a page reached. If it stops at a handoff to a person, identify that handoff. A subsequent event needs its own record.

For a claimed purchase, look for the appropriate business evidence, such as a confirmed order with its date and status. Do not manufacture that status from an assistant's account of where it intended to go next.

- **If you manage the website:** state what the next action requires and where responsibility passes to a person.
- **If you evaluate an agent service:** ask which specific event ended the test and which later events were outside its scope.
- **If you report the result:** preserve the separate task bases so a correct description is not counted as a commercial transaction.

The unobserved purchase outcome is unknown, rather than a zero or a sale. That distinction also protects a useful handoff result: it can demonstrate progress through a defined task without needing to carry a stronger claim about revenue.

### Reported commerce and shopping observations

**Reported.** GetMint's [About page](https://www.getmint.ai/about), marked updated October 2026 and read on 29 October, describes an enterprise platform and specialist services, Content Studio, product presence in AI shopping results and agentic-commerce work across markets including the United States. That reported scope does not supply a matched GetMint-versus-OtterlyAI US checkout test.

OtterlyAI's [Shopping Analytics page](https://otterly.ai/features/ai-shopping-analytics), read on 29 October 2026, describes ChatGPT product and retailer appearances tracked by the country set for one prompt. Its [prompt-monitoring guide](https://help.otterly.ai/search-prompt-monitoring), read on 29 October 2026, distinguishes brand coverage, domain citations, sponsored placements and shopping cards. Retain those output labels when exporting a record; a shopping-card appearance is not an observed order or conversion.

**Reasoned.** A brief using GEO (generative engine optimization), or the buyer terms AEO (answer engine optimization) and AI search visibility, must still name the event it needs. If “transactional” means a product appearing to a shopper ready to buy, a product-appearance record describes discovery. If it means an assistant placing an order, checkout and payment need their own evidence. GetMint names a market; OtterlyAI names a country context for an observation. Neither reported statement nor our 44-of-70 demo-path count establishes purchase reliability through either platform.

Keep any later [pipeline evidence](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/measurement/what-evidence-can-connect-ai-visibility-with-pipeline/) separate from the website-task result.

# How does an AI connector differ from browsing a website?

A connector gives an AI application defined access to data or actions; browsing lets an assistant inspect and use website pages. In the Agent Gap study on 6 October 2026, the assistant found the target pages in all 210 initial tasks, but 163 tasks reached the defined handoff. Those were website-browsing observations, so they cannot be read as a Model Context Protocol (MCP) connection or purchase success rate.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Agent Gap study protocol](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) recorded public website tasks across 70 selected business-to-business software vendors on 6 October 2026. Each vendor had three initial tasks: describe the product, find its pricing page and follow its demo path. The 210 initial sessions are separate from 30 preselected repeat sessions.

Across the initial tasks, the study recorded 206 correct outcomes, 3 incorrect outcomes and 1 unscored outcome. It recorded 163 reached handoffs. Finding a page, correctly describing the result and reaching the task’s destination were separate fields; a handoff did not mean that a form was submitted or a purchase completed. No authenticated connector was tested.

**Reported.** The official [MCP architecture overview](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/2026-07-28/learn/architecture), read 28 October 2026, describes a protocol for exchanging context. A server can expose tools for actions, resources for data and prompts for structured instructions. The protocol does not dictate how an AI application uses that information.

Broadcastwell’s separate [dated connector documentation review](https://broadcastwell.com/best-ai-visibility-tools-with-mcp) covered 17 providers’ public pages on 17 September 2026, with selected later rechecks. It records documented scope and plans, rather than successful connections. Keep that kind of record separate from a browser-task observation too.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** “The assistant can see it” needs a follow-up: through which route, with which information and with permission to do what?

- **If you publish software pages:** make the public product description and destination clear. A readable pricing page can help a browser task without proving that account data is available through a connector.
- **If you use a connector:** inspect its documented fields and actions. A product’s general connector label does not tell you whether it returns the answers, source URLs or dates your report needs.
- **If you buy a service:** ask whether the evidence came from public browsing, documentation or a connection that was actually exercised. Our 210-task result supports the first route, not the other two.

For an AI visibility question, you might need captured answers and their dates. Browsing a public product page would not supply those private account records. Conversely, receiving a metric from a connector does not establish that an assistant can complete the website’s demo path. Choose the route for the task, then retain evidence of what it returned or reached.

### Check the proposed record and permission scope

**Reasoned.** For a supplier proposal, name the record expected back, its identifiers and date fields, the account boundary and whether access is read-only. If actions are offered, identify their approval requirements and how a mistaken request is reported or reversed. Keep one client's records separate from another's.

A successful endpoint response can still omit the answer, source or valid base needed for the decision. Ask for a sample response explaining missing, stale and failed observations. Public page browsing does not supply interface-specific retrieval or action evidence. State whether a demonstration covers browsing, record retrieval or a permitted action, and compare the documented data/permission scope before enabling it.

The Agent Gap destination, correctness and handoff counts above cover public website tasks only. They do not test an authenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) connection or application programming interface (API). A [measurement field comparison](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/measurement/how-do-we-compare-citation-metrics-when-changing-ai-tools/) and [agency publication records](https://broadcastwell.com/best-geo-agencies) concern different kinds of evidence and must keep their own methods.

What should I ask a GEO provider about MCP or API access?

# What evidence should an AI factual-accuracy alert include?

The Absence Index’s [Procore statement record](https://index.broadcastwell.com/vendors/procore/construction-project-management/#wrong-about-you) retains Claude’s 22 September 2026 assertion: “there is no pricing page on their website.” It links the vendor’s [pricing page](https://www.procore.com/pricing), read on 8 October 2026, as contradictory evidence and keeps the question needed to inspect the flag. An accuracy alert should provide that checkable connection rather than a label alone. The record labels the assertion wrong and leaves team review in progress.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** [Wrong About You](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) provides the classification example for an alert record. Its method assessed 2,922 statements about 70 vendors in answers captured on 22 and 23 September 2026, comparing them with vendor pages read on 8 October. It labeled 1,924 true, 113 wrong, five stale and 880 unverifiable. The checkable base was 2,042, including 118 wrong-or-stale statements. Dental practice software accounted for 17 wrong-or-stale statements among 162 checkable statements; legal practice software for 34 among 183. These are dated statement classifications, not monitoring-tool extraction scores. Team review remains in progress. These classes describe reviewed answer claims; they do not measure an alerting product's detection coverage, false alarms or speed. A notification needs its own retained evidence before a reader can assess it.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Google AI Overviews responded to “best construction management software for a small residential builder” on 22 September 2026, run 2, with the fragment “custom quote”. The fragment concerns JobTread. Its published classification record labels the custom-quote claim wrong against the [pricing reference](https://www.jobtread.com/pricing) read on 8 October 2026, with team review in progress. This historical answer wording is not current pricing or independent verification of the product claim.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Request a sample alert before choosing a monitoring arrangement. It should carry the answer's capture date and engine, the exact disputed claim, the cited URL and the dated primary evidence used to assess it. The record also needs a reason for the classification and a clear place to note a correction or unresolved question.

Use the three study labels as a worked routing example. A wrong claim needs evidence of contradiction. A stale claim needs the historical statement and the source showing the later state. An unverifiable claim needs the missing evidence identified; it must not be treated as demonstrated falsehood. The study does not measure any alerting product's ability to detect those cases.

Ask how the supplier distinguishes an observed answer from its own inference about risk. The alert may identify a factual concern without establishing customer harm, lost revenue or a legal violation. If someone has already corrected a source, the record should show that delivery state separately from whether a later answer has changed.

Choose an alert format that a product owner can assess without a second round of detective work. A notification that gives only a score and a vendor name does not provide enough evidence to settle the claim.

- **If you buy monitoring:** ask for one complete alert record and check its source trail.
- **If you own the product fact:** confirm the right classification before approving corrective wording.
- **If you report to a client:** distinguish the observed issue, its review state and any delivered correction.

A tracker may reproduce an engine’s incorrect statement exactly, so extraction agreement does not establish product-fact accuracy. Conversely, a correct fact does not establish company matching or denominator calculations. An alert sample should expose the complete answer, extracted field, alias match, calculation and dated primary passage. Retain all 880 unverifiable statements as unresolved rather than silently converting them to errors or confirmations. The [Study 6 record](../../research/study6-wrong-about-you.md) and [product-quality distinction](../geo-basics/does-being-named-by-ai-prove-product-quality.md) explain those separate checks.

# What should we check when an AI answer gets a fact wrong?

If you have an AI answer with a disputed fact, check the exact statement against the vendor's dated evidence before deciding what needs correction. Wrong About You classified 2 of Procore's 57 extracted statements as wrong: the underlying answers were captured on 22 September 2026 and the vendor's pages read on 8 October. Both flagged records still show team review in progress; they are evidence to inspect, not a claim that a correction has already been completed.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Wrong About You classification method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23270124) records 57 Procore statements: 38 true, two wrong, none stale and 17 unverifiable. These are extracted statements, not the 109 answers that named Procore. The two wrong statements each appeared in one of three runs of the small-general-contractor comparison question.

One Claude record asserted that Procore had no pricing page. The saved vendor page contradicts that assertion. One Google AI Overview record described per-user pricing; the saved Procore source says adding users does not incur a charge. Each flag retains its question, engine, run, answer date, vendor proof and actual review state.

The classifications do not prove that either answer is still being shown or that a proposed repair will change it.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Google AI Overviews responded to “Procore vs Buildertrend, which is better for a small GC” on 22 September 2026, run 2, with the fragment “Per-user/percentage of revenue”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** The Claude flag concerns whether a pricing page exists, not whether it publishes a fixed rate card. A correction should preserve that distinction without inventing a fixed price.

For the Overview flag, the vendor's adding-users passage addresses the per-user assertion. It does not settle every component of a Procore contract.

Procore's 17 unverifiable statements remain unresolved, not wrong. Its zero stale classifications cannot establish that no product fact has changed since capture.

The Claude pricing-page flag records Projul's Procore-versus-Buildertrend comparison as a cited page carrying the disputed statement. That gives the reviewer a named page to inspect alongside Procore's saved pricing page. The study's causing-page label does not prove that Claude read the Projul page as the cause of its answer.

An agency handover needs the in-progress team-review status. Classification, correction review and a changed served answer are separate records; neither Procore flag is marked repaired.

## A separate task-level accuracy record

The [Agent Gap method and release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) records one incorrect initial Describe task among seventy on 6 October 2026. The AppFolio session ended that day with found and reached both true, while correct was false. That is a task classification. It is separate from the Procore statement classifications above; neither base can be used as the other's denominator. It does not identify a clone site as the cause of the error or measure a branded-search defense.

**Reported.** Profound's [FactCheck description](https://www.tryprofound.com/features/answer-engine-insights/factcheck), read on 29 October 2026, describes comparing factual claims with a company-controlled Knowledge Base, displaying source URLs, and offering proposed remediation functions. These are supplier product statements, not a test we conducted. The description distinguishes factual, actionable claims containing one verifiable assertion from subjective statements routed to Sentiment.

Profound says its Knowledge Base can be built by crawling a domain, uploading files or syncing Google Drive and Notion content. It says a claim view displays the ground truth and where it is defined. Those reported functions describe artifacts a reviewer could inspect. They do not independently establish that a particular URL caused a model's answer or that a proposed correction changed it.

**Reasoned.** For a suspected lookalike, keep the exact disputed claim, its cited domain and URL, and the dated official company reference together. A retained URL and a contradictory reference make the claim reviewable. Access alone does not settle accuracy, as the AppFolio task illustrates, and neither that task nor a supplier's attribution feature establishes lookalike causation. The [AI source standard](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/ai-source-standard/) provides a separate public reference for the supporting source.

# Which dental software does ChatGPT recommend?

22 of 30 ChatGPT dental answers named Dentrix, and Open Dental had the same count in our [22 September 2026 panel](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695). Dentrix Ascend appeared in 21. All 30 answers in this engine slice were valid, despite an exclusion elsewhere in the dental collection. Keep those product labels separate: equal naming totals do not establish the same answer-by-answer pattern, clinical quality or a software recommendation.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [September study](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) asked ten dental buyer questions three times on ChatGPT and retained every answer in that engine slice. Dentrix's 22 of 30 gives 73.3 percent, with a descriptive 95 percent Wilson interval of 55.6 to 85.8 percent, a statistical range around the observed share. Collection took place on 22 September 2026, before the 23 September publication.

| Checked vendor | Named in valid ChatGPT answers |
| --- | --- |
| ABELDent | 0 of 30 |
| ACE Dental | 0 of 30 |
| Adit | 0 of 30 |
| CareStack | 14 of 30 |
| Carestream Dental | 0 of 30 |
| Curve Dental | 19 of 30 |
| Dentally | 0 of 30 |
| DentiMax | 0 of 30 |
| Dentrix | 22 of 30 |
| Dentrix Ascend | 21 of 30 |
| Dentrix Enterprise | 1 of 30 |
| DSN | 0 of 30 |

| MacPractice | 0 of 30 |
| Open Dental | 22 of 30 |
| Oryx Dental | 1 of 30 |
| Planet DDS (Denticon) | 12 of 30 |
| Practice-Web | 0 of 30 |
| tab32 | 5 of 30 |

# Which field service software does ChatGPT recommend?

Housecall Pro appeared in 21 of 30 ChatGPT answers in our 22 September 2026 field service panel, but in none of three about commercial mechanical and fire-protection contractors. ServiceTitan appeared in 19 of 30 overall and all three of those commercial answers. The distinction gives you a context for researching names, without proving that either product fits the work.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** Under the [September Index method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), ten field service questions were each observed three times on ChatGPT. All 30 observations were valid. Housecall Pro's 21 appearances are 70.0 percent, with a descriptive 95 percent Wilson uncertainty range of 52.1 to 83.3 percent. Captures are from 22 September 2026; the release date is 23 September.

| Checked vendor | Named in valid ChatGPT answers |
| --- | --- |
| BigChange | 0 of 30 |
| BuildOps | 5 of 30 |
| Commusoft | 0 of 30 |
| FieldEdge | 12 of 30 |
| FieldPulse | 5 of 30 |
| Housecall Pro | 21 of 30 |
| Jobber | 18 of 30 |
| Joblogic | 0 of 30 |
| Kickserv | 2 of 30 |
| RazorSync | 0 of 30 |
| Sera Systems | 0 of 30 |
| Service Fusion | 8 of 30 |
| ServiceM8 | 3 of 30 |
| ServiceMax | 0 of 30 |
| ServicePower | 0 of 30 |
| ServiceTitan | 19 of 30 |
| ServiceTrade | 4 of 30 |
| simpro | 4 of 30 |
| Successware | 0 of 30 |
| Workiz | 6 of 30 |
| WorkWave | 0 of 30 |
| Zuper | 0 of 30 |

The commercial-contractor question named ServiceTrade and BuildOps in all three answers; the small heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) question named Housecall Pro and Jobber in all three. These cuts share the dated panel. Name matching scores neither dispatch, implementation success nor endorsement strength.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), ChatGPT responded to “best field service software for commercial mechanical and fire protection contractors” on 22 September 2026, run 1, and described ServiceTitan with the fragment “Offers commercial service agreements, dispatch, customer portals, and construction workflows.” This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Select the trade-and-size question: a one-person HVAC business and a commercial contractor need separate evaluation. Verify scheduling, service agreements and connections through product documentation or a demonstration. State the trade and product boundary. Retain the dated answer for an omission; the panel explains neither its cause nor a website change that would alter it.

### Jobber's reported UK conditions

**Reported.** Jobber's [Website guide](https://help.getjobber.com/en/articles/website-marketing-tools/) and [Dedicated Phone Number guide](https://help.getjobber.com/en/articles/dedicated-phone-number/), updated 28 October and read on 30 October 2026 UTC, name the United Kingdom for Receptionist and phone-number routes. Receptionist chat is listed with all plans; phone and text replies need an applicable add-on or Plus plan, and website publication needs an active supported subscription.

Website chat can answer questions, submit service requests and, with Online Booking configured, book jobs. A boiler-service request is separate from a completed booking. Phone and text require a dedicated number even alongside an existing number. UK number setup requires a selected plan and an administrator, excludes trials and cannot change the dedicated number after selection.

Receptionist dashboard and settings access is administrator-only; administrators or users with Marketing Suite permission can generate and publish a website. Website permission does not confer Receptionist settings access.

**Reasoned.** Jobber's 18 table appearances count the vendor once per answer, not UK access, Receptionist performance or bookings. Read the [field-service buyer questions](https://index.broadcastwell.com/questions/field-service-management/) separately from dated product conditions.

The [Manual on valid measurement](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/) explains the event and base.

### Monitoring the contractor and naming its software are different tasks

**Reported.** The [Semrush AI Visibility Toolkit guide](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1493-ai-visibility-toolkit), read on 30 October 2026, describes weekly Brand Performance reports for one domain, a language and a location, including cities. Its separate daily Prompt Tracking names ChatGPT and Google AI Mode.

The [seoClarity Overview description](https://www.seoclarity.net/research/ai-overviews-impact), updated 23 October 2025 and read on 29 October 2026, describes AI Overview keyword filters, linked-domain checks and search engine results page (SERP) Previews. Semrush's AI Mode wording does not establish an Overview-reference function.

**Reasoned.** AEO (answer engine optimization), GEO (generative engine optimization) and AI search visibility monitoring concern a different tool class. The Jobber count concerns a software vendor, not a plumbing, roofing or heating contractor named to a household. A contractor report needs its domain, service area and question set. This panel tests neither monitoring tools nor local-contractor visibility.

# Which insurance agency software does ChatGPT recommend?

An overall total can conceal that decision, so open the relevant question instead of treating all agency-management work as interchangeable.

# Which transportation software does ChatGPT recommend?

Freight-broker and enterprise-shipper questions produced different ChatGPT names in our [transportation panel](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695). Descartes appeared in all three broker answers, but in no enterprise-shipper answer; Blue Yonder appeared in all three of the latter. Descartes' overall 12 of 30 belongs to that mixed question set, captured on 22 September 2026, rather than a recommendation for every freight operation.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [September Index release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) contains ten transportation questions, observed three times each on ChatGPT. All 30 answers were usable. The questions distinguish brokers, carriers and shippers, as well as named-product comparisons and general buying criteria. Captures are dated 22 September 2026, with publication on 23 September.

Descartes appeared in 40.0 percent of these answers. Its descriptive 95 percent Wilson uncertainty range is 24.6 to 57.7 percent; this fixed broker, carrier and shipper question set is not a representative survey of transportation buyers.

TMS means transportation management system.

| Checked vendor | Named in valid ChatGPT answers |
| --- | --- |
| 3PL Systems | 0 of 30 |
| Alvys | 9 of 30 |
| AscendTMS | 8 of 30 |
| Axon Software | 0 of 30 |
| Blue Yonder | 6 of 30 |
| Descartes | 12 of 30 |
| Descartes 3G TMS | 3 of 30 |
| Descartes Aljex | 10 of 30 |
| e2open | 5 of 30 |
| FreightPOP | 1 of 30 |
| Infios (MercuryGate) | 6 of 30 |
| IntelliTrans | 0 of 30 |
| Kuebix by FreightWise | 0 of 30 |
| Manhattan Active TM | 0 of 30 |
| McLeod Software | 0 of 30 |
| Oracle Transportation Management | 6 of 30 |
| PCS Software | 0 of 30 |
| Princeton TMX | 0 of 30 |
| Revenova | 3 of 30 |
| Rose Rocket | 4 of 30 |
| SAP Transportation Management | 6 of 30 |
| Tai TMS | 8 of 30 |
| Trimble Transportation | 0 of 30 |
| Turvo | 7 of 30 |
| Uber Freight TMS | 2 of 30 |

Sixteen of the 25 checked vendors appeared at least once. The table is alphabetical, retaining all nine zero rows. It is limited to the release's checked names and recorded aliases, so a zero does not mean an answer contained no other transportation product. Several names can occur in the same answer.

The broker and enterprise examples are three-answer subsets of this panel. Blue Yonder's category count was six, and its three enterprise appearances belong inside that total. Counting these examples again would inflate the panel.

[Every figure comes from the published method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), ChatGPT responded to “What are the best alternatives to MercuryGate?” on 22 September 2026, run 1, with the fragment “**Descartes 3G TMS**”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Decide whether you are evaluating brokerage work, carrier operations or shipper planning before reading the counts. A broad transportation label can conceal that distinction. Open the relevant question record and read the explanation around each name, including any qualifications around the comparison.

Write down the work a candidate must support, then seek product evidence for it. For example, if a particular handoff between teams matters, ask for a demonstration of that handoff under your conditions. The twelve Descartes appearances do not verify an integration, a contract term or an operating result.

When presenting this finding to a colleague, retain the engine, question and date. A category total can describe how often a checked name occurred across this fixed collection. It cannot explain the engine's selection process or turn a new answer into the same observation.

Our [construction criterion record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271935) retains ChatGPT’s phrase “software that fits how your projects actually run” before any vendor name in a 22 September 2026 answer about choosing construction software. Turn that stated decision into the page’s question, then put product evidence beside the workflow claim you can support. This is an observed answer criterion with coding review in progress, not a verified buyer need or an experiment showing an answer-page effect.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [published Study 7 record](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23271935) connects construction criteria to the answer spans from which they were extracted. Workflow fit was one of 92 criteria in that category. Its frequency of 17 in 149 answers is 11.4 percent, with a descriptive Wilson 95 percent interval from 7.2 to 17.5 percent.

Criteria were extracted before the first vendor name. One request-limit answer was excluded from this derived collection; its base therefore differs from the original 150-answer Index category. Coding review remains in progress. The method describes AI-stated criteria and dated vendor-page comparisons, not an experiment on a new answer page.

Two separate construction criteria make possible page questions more specific. Clear pricing basis and included features appeared in 5/149 included answers: two ChatGPT and three Claude returns to the pricing question on 22 September 2026, with a published interval of 1.4% to 7.6%. RFI (request for information), submittal and field-report workflow requirements appeared in 9/149 answers from that capture. These criteria and the 17/149 workflow-fit count are non-additive; they do not identify distinct extra answers. Coding review remains in progress. None measures e-commerce visibility, generated-page quality or a causal page effect. The software examples distinguish per-user, per-project and construction-volume pricing.

**Reasoned.** Preserve the buyer task before choosing a title or product example. A criterion observed across answers may help you decide what evidence to gather, but it cannot establish that your product meets the criterion.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Perplexity responded to “best construction management software for subcontractors” on 22 September 2026, run 2, with the fragment “**field operations, bidding, payments, or all-in-one job management**”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

For a GEO (generative engine optimization) answer page, keep the buyer decision, the observed reason for examining it and the product evidence distinct. Buyers may call this AEO (answer engine optimization) or AI search visibility; the product source still needs to establish the workflow you describe.

Open with the answer your sources support. Explain the users, task and product scope it covers. If only part of the question is settled, say what remains unresolved.

For workflow copy, establish the task, supported path, prerequisites and boundaries with product evidence. Keep private personal and client details out of the public answer. Extend an existing page when it already resolves the question; otherwise state the new decision and link broader guidance. Check served text and links after publication without treating delivery as a measured AI-output effect. Keep the [measurement boundary](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/) explicit.

- **For a product team:** establish the product facts before writing the answer.
- **For an editor:** keep one decision, one supported scope and visible evidence boundaries.

**Reported.** Google’s [merchant-listing guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing), read on 30 October 2026, applies to a purchasable product or its variants, requires an active Offer price above zero and a three-letter ISO 4217 currency, and specifies a distinct URL per currency. Its [product-snippet guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product-snippet), also read on 30 October, covers editorial product reviews. Explain the purchased pack, variant, quantity, term, modules and included access beside the amount. An active price may appear in offers.price or priceSpecification; when both specify one, offers.price takes precedence.

Jobber’s [website guide](https://help.getjobber.com/en/articles/website-marketing-tools/), read on 30 October 2026 UTC, describes using a business story to suggest service pages and create content. It does not establish verified construction-dataset comparisons or a bulk-template pipeline. Semrush’s [toolkit guide](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1493-ai-visibility-toolkit), read that day, describes AI Search Site Audit checks for potential crawling blockers. Those checks do not verify an RFI or submittal feature claim. Google’s [AI features guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, separately requires indexing and snippet eligibility for supporting links.

# How should I use robots.txt to control AI crawler access?

Broadcastwell's [robots.txt](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/robots.txt), served on 2 November 2026, has separate Googlebot and Google-Extended groups, each with `Allow: /`. Choose the group for the crawler and use you intend to control, then set the relevant path rule. Our file records a declared access policy; it does not establish a visit, crawler compliance, training use or an answer citation. The provider's documentation is needed to identify each crawler's purpose.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Agent Gap task method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) recorded three public website tasks across 70 software vendors. It recorded 206 correct results, three incorrect and one unscored across 210 initial sessions. Thirty repeat sessions were separate. The study did not compare crawler policies, authenticate bot identities or test whether a rules change caused an answer to cite a page.

In the 6 October 2026 Agent Gap collection, all 210 initial tasks found a target page and 163 reached the defined endpoint.

**Reported.** Google's [AI feature guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read 28 October 2026, identifies Googlebot rules as the crawl control for Search, including its AI features. Google-Extended governs different uses, including training and grounding in other Google products. Google's [robots.txt introduction](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots/intro), read the same date, explains that crawler instructions depend on crawler cooperation and do not secure private content.

### A separate description-task count

The [Agent Gap protocol](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23197560) records reached endpoints in 67 of 70 initial Describe tasks on 6 October 2026. Those tasks concerned vendors' public websites. They did not identify the requests as OAI-SearchBot, GPTBot or an Anthropic robot, or test the effect of a robots rule. This description-task cut is part of the broader task collection above; it must not be added to that collection's endpoint total. A reached endpoint is not a verified crawler visit.

### Provider purposes and the host being controlled

**Reported.** OpenAI's [bot documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), read on 29 October 2026, separates OAI-SearchBot for search from GPTBot for training. It describes ChatGPT-User as acting on user requests, separately from automatic search crawling. [Anthropic's crawler article](https://support.anthropic.com/en/articles/8896518-does-anthropic-crawl-data-from-the-web-and-how-can-site-owners-block-the-crawler), also read on 29 October 2026, distinguishes ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot and Claude-User and gives their purposes and robots.txt instructions.

Anthropic distinguishes Claude-User's user-directed retrieval from Claude-SearchBot's search purpose. Its guide places robots.txt controls on the site or subdomain concerned. A documentation subdomain therefore needs its own addressed rule record, rather than an assumption that the homepage's file controls that separate host.

OpenAI's [search help article](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read on 29 October 2026, also asks publishers to allow traffic from its published searchbot IP (Internet Protocol) addresses at the host. A robots permission and a host restriction are separate checks; changing one does not verify the other. The bot's documented purpose, the declared policy and any actual observed visit remain distinct evidence.

**Reasoned.** If the intended policy restricts training while permitting search, inspect the separate named tokens. For an agency managing a documentation subdomain, record the intended purpose, exact bot and inspected address. A later answer that omits a company would need its own answer record; it would not identify which robot requested the page.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** First write the access decision in plain language. You may want a public source available to search while choosing a different policy for another use. An undifferentiated instruction to block AI cannot express those separate decisions reliably.

Identify the provider's documented crawler token and the exact paths affected. Review the existing rules before adding a new group; a broad rule may cover more public content than the page you had in mind. Test representative allowed and disallowed URLs against the intended rule interpretation, then inspect the actual served robots.txt file.

Keep hosting and access controls in the same review. A page permitted by robots.txt can still be unavailable because of its server or delivery settings. A disallow instruction is also different from a request to remove a URL from search results. Use the provider's documented indexing or snippet controls for that separate goal.

Preserve a dated before-and-after rule record and the reason for the change. Verification should show which published rule applies to which URL. It cannot certify that every crawler obeyed it, that an assistant completed a task or that a future answer will include your company.

See [the Manual’s citation chapter](../../who-gets-cited.md).

- **For a site owner:** separate search access from other provider uses.
- **For a developer:** test the named token and affected paths before changing the served file.
- **For an agency:** report policy delivery separately from observed requests or answers.

**Reported.** OpenAI's [bot documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), read on 29 October 2026, separates OAI-SearchBot for search from GPTBot for training. # Can an AI answer cite a company without naming it?

Yes. In [Volume II](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21586091), nine of 85 companies received at least one own-domain citation while their brands had no naming observations across their ten answers. Those answers were captured from July 18 to 23, 2026, under independent naming and citation rules. A cited publisher could therefore supply evidence without appearing as a product option. The September Index uses a different citation definition.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Volume II scoring method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21586091) recorded two independent binary events for each answer: the company's brand named and its own domain cited. The sample covered 85 selected B2B (business-to-business) software companies, ten questions each, with one run per question on one engine using live web search. Nine companies had zero naming observations and at least one own-domain citation.

This historical definition matters. The [September Index's scoring method](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) instead requires the vendor to be named and its domain cited in the same answer. You cannot use the nine historical cases as if they were exceptions to that later event definition.

The July result does not establish why an engine used a source or which page change would make its publisher a candidate.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

**Reported.** Google’s [AI features guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 29 October 2026, requires a supporting page to be indexed and eligible for a Search snippet. It advises keeping Business Profile information current, without requiring a special AI file or new schema type. OpenAI’s [Search help](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-searching-the-web-with-chatgpt), read that day, describes location-sensitive local results and says approximate IP-derived location can affect them; specifying a city, neighborhood or postal code can clarify the area. Its [crawler documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/bots), also read that day, separates OAI-SearchBot search access from GPTBot training access. Host or content-delivery-network restrictions also affect access.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Inspect the cited page separately from the answer's proposed products. A page may supply evidence about a category, a workflow or another company. Its appearance among sources does not require the answer to describe its publisher as a vendor option.

The useful report keeps both fields and their definitions. If you receive a citation total from a different release or platform, first check whether naming is a prerequisite. Otherwise an apparent contradiction may be only a change in what is counted.

- **If you publish the source:** preserve the cited URL and the answer that used it. Do not label the event as a recommendation without reading the context.
- **If you report visibility:** for GEO (generative engine optimization), also called AEO (answer engine optimization) or AI search visibility, state the release and citation rule beside the number, especially when comparing historical data.
- **If you buy software:** separate the publishers of supporting material from the products the answer proposes for your need.

The same discipline applies when a domain supports several products. A domain match identifies a source relationship under a rule; it does not, by itself, establish which product claim was supported or whether that claim was sound.

A local service page illustrates that distinction: a vehicle-glass safety article can supply evidence without recommending its publisher as a nearby windshield operator. Keep the requested town and actual service area beside the answer, then inspect whether a citation points to the shop’s service page, another operator or general advice. These are reasoned checks, not measured auto-glass outcomes. See [valid measurement](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/) for the separation between an observation and an intervention claim.

# Which review sites for GEO should a buyer compare?

Compare Clutch's client accounts with G2's software-product reviews, and treat an agency's ranked list as a different kind of evidence. In [our audit dated 17 September 2026](https://broadcastwell.com/best-geo-agencies-lists-audited), 29 of 32 agency-list rows marked Yes for the publisher appearing on its own list. Before relying on a recommendation for this work, check who published it and whether you are reading a client's experience, a product review or an editorial selection.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

GEO (generative engine optimization), AEO (answer engine optimization) and AI search visibility are buyer terms for this work. The published checks below concern the evidence a supplier provides.

## What we measured

Measured: our [32-list audit](https://broadcastwell.com/best-geo-agencies-lists-audited) reads each list page once. A publisher with two pages appears twice. The [public row receipt](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/assets/library/agency-list-audit-2026-09-17.json) retains 29 Yes entries, two No entries and a separate Parent company listed entry in its own-list column; that last status was not converted to Yes for this count.

The [six published criteria](https://broadcastwell.com/best-geo-agencies-lists-audited#how-scored) concern disclosure, selection criteria, claim sources, dates, prices and corrections. They describe what a reader could inspect on each page. Broadcastwell publishes the comparison, sells related services and is outside its scored table. This count does not measure agency quality or how representative a review is.

Reported: [Clutch's verification guidance](https://help.clutch.co/en/knowledge/where-is-clients-online-review), read on 29 October 2026, says submitted reviews go through verification before publication. It also says the displayed review date is when the client started it, which can differ from completion and publication dates. Keep that distinction when checking whether an account is recent.

G2's [community guidelines](https://legal.g2.com/community-guidelines), read on 29 October 2026, distinguish Validated Reviewer from Current User. The first label concerns identity authentication; the second means the reviewer uploaded a screenshot of product use. Neither label states that a GEO campaign changed an AI answer.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Read a Clutch review date as the help page defines it: the day the client began the review, rather than necessarily its publication day. The verification process and that displayed date describe different events. If you need an account of recent work, read the project dates in the review instead of assigning that role to the date above it.

The two No rows in our September audit belong to AEO Vision and The AI Journal. They answer whether the publisher appeared on its own list, without establishing independence or client satisfaction. Both rows have a Partial for Links sources. A No in the self-inclusion column therefore does not establish that the page supplies strong evidence for its choices.

Nutshell has the separate Parent company listed status. It stays outside the 29 Yes count. That distinction catches a different disclosure question from matching the publisher's own name: the list can include a related company even when the publisher name itself is absent.

### Inspect the list an answer actually cites

**Reported.** OpenAI's [ChatGPT Search guidance](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/9237897-chatgpt-search), read on 29 October 2026, describes inline citations and a Sources button for supporting links. Google's [AI-feature guidance](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read that day, includes keeping Business Profile information current and matching structured data to visible page text.

**Reasoned.** Open the specific cited list and compare its entry with the sentence in the answer. Retain the publisher, selection date and, for a local list, the city in its title. A different city is a mismatch to record; changing the business's actual service area to imitate the list would change a business fact to fit a source.

Use the disclosure questions with their limits intact. A publisher appearing on its list and a related parent company appearing there are different relationships. The agency-list audit above did not measure local rankings, client outcomes or ChatGPT's source-selection cause, and applying its inspection questions to a local page is reasoned advice. It does not establish that the local list caused an answer or that copying its ordering will change one.

For an outdated phone number, opening time or service-area statement, identify the exact claim. Reconcile the accurate public business detail with its structured data and Business Profile, preserving the cited page's date. An ordering on a historical list is not a current business record.

Keep the [Manual on valid measurement](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/valid-measurement/) with the record when deciding what its event and base establish.

Study method: [v1.1](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology).

# How do Google AI Overviews affect website visibility?

1,352 checked-name appearances across 415 retained Google AI Overviews answers show one form of visibility: being named inside an answer. Our [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), collected on 22 and 23 September 2026, did not measure whether that exposure increased or reduced visits to the named companies’ websites.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Index design](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) covers fourteen software categories, with ten buyer questions and three repeats per engine. Of 420 scheduled Overview answers, 415 were retained and five excluded. Its name counts describe the checked vendors in retained answer text. They are not 1,352 visitors, and the 415-answer base is not a website audience.

**Reported.** Google's [AI-feature impression report help](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139), read on 2 November 2026, describes a separate view of site-link impressions in AI Overviews and AI Mode. The same traffic remains part of Web performance data. The documented AI view reports impressions; an answer naming a company does not supply a click total.

**Reasoned.** In GEO (generative engine optimization), also called AEO (answer engine optimization) or AI search visibility, a named company, a cited domain and a clicked link are different events. A vendor may be visible in prose without an own-domain link, or its website may support an answer without receiving a recommendation. The Index can describe the first two kinds of observation; it cannot convert them into a measured website impact.

### Two historical answer fragments

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Google AI Overviews answered the general contractor (GC) question “best construction software for a small GC that needs estimating and scheduling without Procore complexity” on 22 September 2026, run 2, with the fragment “Feature / Need | JobTread | Contractor Foreman”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

A separate Overview return to that question on 22 September 2026, run 1, describes scheduling with “Gantt-style or calendar drag-and-drop views that link directly to your budget items”. It is a generic selection criterion, not a vendor-specific tested feature or ad evidence.

## What this means for you

Look at Procore. In the construction category, its name appears in 21 of 30 retained Overview answers. That engine-specific count describes answer text; the vendor's separate pooled record reports 109 named appearances and 30 own-domain citations across 150 answers on five engines. The three figures refer to different columns or bases, so none supplies a website visitor count.

The named source destinations make the difference visible. The construction export records capterra.com as a cited host in 34 of its 150 pooled answers, while Procore's vendor record identifies procore.com and learn.procore.com as its cited domains. A directory-host observation and a vendor's own-domain citation are distinct records, even when both concern construction software.

For a website, the AI-feature impression report and the Web click report describe different recorded events. Google's inspected [report help](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16984139) offers page, country, date and device breakdowns for AI-feature impressions. Analytics supplies separate site-behavior and conversion records. The September Index instead retains names, question-level counts and cited domains; its Procore row has no click, session or conversion field.

### Paid placements are a separate observation

**Reported.** Google's [ads guide](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/18826097?hl=en), read on 30 October 2026, says Overview and AI Mode ads carry a Sponsored label and are visually distinct from organic content. Ads can appear within or alongside commercially relevant responses; ordinary Search ads can appear above or below an Overview. The guide says paid advertising does not influence the organic AI response. That statement does not measure where people click.

Google describes direct matching to a commercial query and contextual matching to both query and generated response. An exploratory query can therefore lead to a Sponsored placement through the response's commercial context. This describes Google's matching rules, not an observed association in our panel.

Campaign reports aggregate impressions, clicks, conversions and cost from queries triggering AI-feature ads alongside other eligible activity. Those queries also enter the aggregate search-terms report. Neither report isolates an organic-click change for a particular Overview. Our Index measured neither ad exposure nor changes in organic clicks; its name totals establish no traffic gain, loss or placement effect.

# What is a Google AI Overview?

A Google AI Overview is an AI-generated part of Search that helps explain a topic and links to supporting web pages. It does not appear for every search: in our 4 August 2026 study, 258 of 280 main Google searches returned an Overview and 22 did not. That dated sample illustrates the distinction between running a search and receiving an AI answer.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Reported.** Google’s [AI-feature guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 28 October 2026, describes topic explanations with supporting links. It says Overviews appear when its systems judge them additive to classic Search; our study did not reverse-engineer that rule.

**Measured.** The [Volume III method and data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21789120) record main searches separately from repeats: 280 main searches on 4 August 2026, with 258 Overviews and 22 without one. A search without an Overview differs from a brand omitted inside an existing answer.

**Reasoned.** Search can show other results without an Overview. These historical counts from a particular question collection do not estimate arbitrary queries’ current probabilities or explain Google’s decisions.

[Our answer-study method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

### A separate September collection

**Measured.** The [September Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) scheduled fourteen software categories, ten buyer questions and three repeats per engine on 22 and 23 September 2026: 415 retained Overview answers from 420 targets. Four exclusions recorded no Overview; the fifth, veterinary-practice-management result said valid results could not be obtained. Keep those states and the August population separate.

The 415 retained answers contained 1,352 appearances of checked vendor names; several names can occur in one answer. These answer-text events do not measure ad placement, auction eligibility, advertiser payments or spend.

### Two historical answer fragments

For a business-intelligence platform evaluation question, a [retained Google Overview](https://github.com/Broadcastwell/state-of-geo-2026/blob/main/volume-iii/data/raw.csv) from 4 August 2026 reads: “A structured evaluation framework helps enterprises compare platforms effectively:”. A separate [Overview answer](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), captured on 22 September 2026 for a small residential builder, describes JobTread with “Sales, estimating, digital takeoffs, budgeting, customer invoices, and vendor/subcontractor portals.” These are historical answer fragments, not feature verification, an ad observation or an explanation of aggregate counts.

## What this means for you

Record whether an Overview appears before counting its names and links. Keep ordinary Search results outside the answer count. Google’s guide requires indexing and snippet eligibility for supporting pages; meeting those conditions does not guarantee inclusion.

### Historical France launch

**Reported.** Google announced AI Overviews and AI Mode in France on 22 July 2026. Its [launch announcement](https://blog.google/intl/fr-fr/nouveautes-produits/explorez-obtenez-des-r%25C3%25A9ponses/recherche-ia-apercus-mode/), read on 29 October 2026, describes desktop, mobile and Google-app availability, with Overviews displayed when its systems find them useful. It distinguishes short Overviews from longer Mode conversations; count a subsequent Mode answer separately. The [Overview help page](https://support.google.com/websearch/answer/14901683), read on 29 October 2026, is a separate reference.

The France article’s publisher-control account is historical. Google’s [control help](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/16908024), read on 2 November 2026, describes worldwide participation controls and possible inheritance from a parent property. That later documentation neither changes the French launch date nor guarantees an Overview. Keep participation control separate from ordinary ranking.

**Reasoned.** Neither collection tested French availability. Retain the query and observed surface; an absent Overview neither contradicts the launch nor estimates that reader’s probability.

### Ads and answer text

**Reported.** Google’s [ads guide](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/18826097?hl=en), read on 30 October 2026, distinguishes Sponsored ads from organic AI content and says payment does not influence organic responses. It separates in-Overview ads from standard Search ads above or below the answer; layouts may change. It describes in-answer ads in English in listed markets, versus above/below ads across the 200-plus countries and territories and languages where Overviews are available. These dated conditions do not establish an in-answer placement for every query or country.

The guide includes AI-surface ad metrics in aggregate standard campaign reports, rather than an isolated Overview-placement report. Keep the Sponsored label and answer boundary when assessing a screenshot. A reported ad click and a name inside answer prose are different events. The [measurement boundary](../../valid-measurement.md) applies here too.

# What is Google AI Mode?

For a question requiring an extended comparison, Google's [AI-feature guide](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 2 November 2026, describes AI Mode as a Search experience for exploration, reasoning and comparisons. One [22 September 2026 construction question](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), about software for a small residential builder, returned Buildertrend in all three AI Mode answers. That is an example from the named experience, without testing product suitability or describing everything AI Mode can do. The provider's feature description and our captured result serve different purposes.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Reported.** Google's [AI-feature documentation](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/ai-features), read on 28 October 2026, explains AI Mode's exploration and comparison role. Both AI Mode and AI Overviews may issue related searches across subtopics and data sources. Google says the two can use different models and techniques, so their responses and links can vary.

**Measured.** The September construction category contained ten buyer questions and three scheduled runs per engine. For the question about construction-management software for a small residential builder, AI Mode named Procore in all three valid answers. The descriptive 95% Wilson interval is 43.9% to 100.0%, a wide range despite the complete observed count.

The [September release](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695), published 23 September 2026, supplies that question-level naming result. It does not supply an engine-specific own-domain citation count in this comparison.

**Reasoned.** A product name in three answers is evidence of those mentions, without establishing a product recommendation, purchase or future presence.

[Every figure comes from the published method, v1.1.](https://broadcastwell.com/methodology)

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Google AI Mode responded to “best construction management software for a small residential builder” on 22 September 2026, run 3, with the fragment “Buildertrend and JobTread”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

Label AI Mode separately from AI Overviews in a report. Combining them under “Google AI” would hide which experience produced the result and make a later comparison harder to interpret.

Keep the original question beside a screenshot or count. A complex comparison and a broad category search ask for different things, even when the same product appears in both.

Open the supporting links when a product fact matters to your decision. The ability to explore a question does not make every generated statement current or supported, and the naming count above cannot answer that factual question for you.

# How do AI visibility providers differ in sampling answers and measuring share of voice?

13 checked-name appearances in three Perplexity returns show why an answer total and a mention total need different labels. That is the scaling-small-sales-team CRM (customer relationship management) row in our [22 September 2026 Index](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695). Suede reports persona-based capture; Profound defines several denominators; AthenaHQ-supported research publishes eligible-cohort and source-counting rules.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The [Index method and data](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695) retain three Perplexity returns to one CRM question. HubSpot CRM, Pipedrive, Salesforce Sales Cloud and Zoho CRM each appear in all three; Freshsales in one: 13 checked-name appearances across three answers, counting each supplier once per return. The panel does not establish provider sampling weights, coverage or account-specific totals.

Claude’s same-release total is 2,039 checked-name appearances across 420 valid answers: 14 categories, ten questions each, three returns per engine on 22 September 2026. Several vendors may appear per answer. This is neither a brand’s answer percentage, a UK sample nor evidence of account access.

**Reported.** Suede’s Platform page, read on 30 October 2026, describes daily persona-specific questions, captured responses, stance, sentiment and sources, but gives no share-of-voice denominator or sampling weights. Profound’s AEI (Answer Engine Insights) guide, read on 29 October 2026, defines Visibility against responses containing a brand, and Share of Voice against total brand mentions across responses. AthenaHQ’s FAQ (frequently asked questions), read that day, lists mentions, citations, share of voice and content-gap functions. The separately Athena-supported Answer Signal method, version 1.0 of August 2026 and read on 29 October 2026, specifies observation windows, eligible cohorts and normalized root domains. Unless otherwise stated, it excludes flagged responses and deleted records, and uses like-for-like cohorts for longitudinal comparisons.

**Reasoned.** The 13/3 row shows vendor-name presences exceeding answer counts. For GEO (generative engine optimization), also called AEO (answer engine optimization) or AI search visibility, compare each provider’s share-of-voice definition with that unit.

### Two historical answer fragments

For the scaling-small-sales-team question, a [Perplexity answer](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1) captured on 22 September 2026 includes “**Pipedrive**, **Pipeline CRM**, **Zoho CRM**, and **Salesforce Starter Suite**”. A ChatGPT return to that question on the same date reads “Pipedrive, HubSpot, Zoho CRM, and Close”. The ChatGPT table includes product-pricing links. Both are historical answer fragments, not verified functionality or explanations of aggregate counts.

## What this means for you

Semrush’s [toolkit guide](https://www.semrush.com/kb/1493-ai-visibility-toolkit), read on 30 October 2026 UTC, lists UK coverage and daily rolling updates for Visibility Overview, Competitor Research and Prompt Research. Brand Performance uses configured location/language and updates weekly; Prompt Tracking updates daily; AI Search Site Audit runs on demand. Worldwide/regional Overview filtering differs from a configured UK brand report. The toolkit FAQ requires a paid subscription and allocated corporate-user limit; its no-trial rule differs from the generic footer invitation.

One comparison in the [seoClarity article](https://www.seoclarity.net/research/ai-overviews-impact), updated on 23 October 2025 and read on 29 October 2026, covers UK desktop Overviews from September 2024 to September 2025. It describes an Overview filter in SERP Features (search engine results page features), referenced-site checks and returned content in SERP Previews. These concern Google source links, not Claude brand mentions. Keep each engine, unit, location and date distinct, as in [the Profound/seoClarity comparison](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/answers/geo-basics/how-do-profound-and-seo-clarity-compare-for-tracking-brand-coverage-in/).

**Measured.** The [CRM CSV](https://index.broadcastwell.com/data/crm-2026-09.csv) records Close in 3 of 30 ChatGPT answers on 22 September 2026, across ten questions with three repeats. All three belong to [one scaling-team question](https://index.broadcastwell.com/questions/crm/which-crm-options-work-well-for-a-small-sales-team-that-is-scaling/); the other nine questions have no Close observations. Each ChatGPT repeat shortlisted Close alongside Pipedrive, HubSpot and Zoho. Valid non-naming answers remain in the base. Across five engines, Close appears in 12 of 150 answers. Those observations do not establish vendor popularity or product quality.

A single-question service could reproduce the same three mentions without covering the thirty-answer panel. Specify questions, repeats, engines, countries/languages, retained text, source links, exports and review work when comparing scopes. The release records no supplier fees, staff time or repair costs. Product-pricing citations require their own billing-unit and dated-source checks; naming counts cannot price that work. [Measurement noise](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/measurement-noise/) is a separate consideration.

# What evidence can connect AI visibility with pipeline?

If you connect AI visibility with pipeline, retain the dated answer, visit, buyer account and opportunity records, with a stated rule for joining them. Our [published AI Source Standard](https://docs.broadcastwell.com/ai-source-standard/), served on 2 November 2026, puts answer observations, referral visits, buyer self-reports and qualified opportunities in separate columns. That is a reporting framework, without a measured chain from an answer to a sale. Missing connections must remain unknown.

Observed answers on stated dates, not a ranking.

## What we measured

**Measured.** The September Absence Index records answers, not customer journeys. Housecall Pro’s field service collection retained 150 valid answers from ten buyer questions, repeated three times on ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and Google AI Mode. The answers were captured 22 September 2026 and published 23 September under [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22907695](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22907695).

Its 108 named answers give 72.0 percent, with a Wilson 95 percent interval of 64.3 to 78.6 percent. Its own domain was cited in 43 of 150 answers, or 28.7 percent. A citation can provide a possible route to a site, but the record does not show that a buyer followed it. We cannot calculate a lead rate or revenue contribution from these answer counts.

The Manual’s [AI source attribution standard](../../ai-source-standard.md) provides the framework for reading business evidence alongside these observations. The process below is a reasoned reporting approach, not a measured conversion result for Housecall Pro.

### One retained answer

In one retained [answer record](https://zenodo.org/records/22907695/files/answers-2026-09.jsonl?download=1), Claude answered the heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) question “what is the best field service software for a small HVAC company” on 22 September 2026, run 3, with the fragment “**Jobber** and **Housecall Pro**”. This historical wording is an answer observation, not independent verification of the product claim or an explanation of the aggregate count.

## What this means for you

**Reasoned.** Keep a separate record for each part of the proposed connection. The answer record names the question, engine, date, company role and cited page. A visit record contains the source information actually received and the period observed. A buyer’s account records what that person says influenced them. An opportunity or sale needs its own business record and status.

Connect records only where the evidence permits it. A recognized referral label supports a narrower statement than a complete influence history. A buyer may remember using an AI service without identifying the answer or arriving through its link. Record that account as a self-report rather than turning it into a recovered browsing trail.

- **If you run marketing:** publish the connection rule with the result. State which records were matched, which came from buyer reports and which still have an unknown source.
- **If you manage sales:** retain the buyer’s actual account and the dated opportunity record. Do not replace an unknown source with AI because the company appeared in a separate answer check.
- **If you sell software:** distinguish the question where you were named from the buyer’s later decision. The answer may concern a need that never became a purchase.
- **If you report for an agency:** for GEO (generative engine optimization) or AEO (answer engine optimization), show AI search visibility, referrals and opportunities in separate columns. Name a missing record instead of treating it as either a sale or a zero.

A before-and-after chart also needs care. Publication, answer changes and opportunities can occur in the same period without showing that one caused the next. Keep their dates and other known changes visible. If the join cannot be supported, report the observed answer result and leave the pipeline contribution unknown.
